label: main season
summary: Recommend clearance for sign-off: E1 is an in-area past-accident database record, classified as weak indirect evidence because its date and location have not been verified. National criteria make this record a clearance target after the first NTS visit and prohibit release by NTS alone; technical survey is unavailable. The reports of long-term safe use and the team's observations support absence but do not override that requirement.
flags: E1 has no date or other detail, and its location has not been checked on the ground; retain this uncertainty for sign-off.
E3 covers paths and field edges walked, not necessarily the entire forest area.

checks.detail: Every item of the evidence log is in the register.
The national criteria provide no technical survey, so clearance takes its place; evidence to target: E1.

E1.quote: The national mine action database records one or more past landmine accidents inside this area.
E1.note: Unverified desk-study record with no date or ground-checked location; it suggests possible contamination but does not confirm it.

E2.quote: We have hunted and fished along these streams for 22 years. Nobody has found anything, and nobody has been hurt.
E2.note: A first-hand land user reports 22 years of safe use, supporting absence and providing context that may explain the unchecked, undated record; it does not override the national rule that this recorded accident requires clearance after visit one.

E3.quote: The survey team walked the paths and field edges of the area and saw no items, signs, fencing or other marks of contamination.
E3.note: The team's own observation found no contamination indicators on the paths and field edges it walked; this is evidence of absence, not proof about unobserved land.

E4.quote: A woodcutter said he has cut firewood and timber in the area every year for the past 13 years, and has never found anything or heard of an accident there.
E4.note: A first-hand user reports 13 years of safe use and no known accident, which provides context potentially explaining the unchecked record; the national accident-record criterion still requires clearance after the first visit.
